walkthroughs.body_html:
The greenhouse effect is natural.

But extra CO2 from cars, power and industry strengthens it.

Extra heat melts ice, raises seas and shifts weather.

Eutrophication harms rivers and lakes.

Fertiliser feeds algal blooms; blooms block light and starve plants below.

When the algae die, decomposers use up oxygen and fish die.

Biodiversity has several enemies.

Land clearance, overfishing and invasive species all hit native species.

UK grey squirrels have replaced reds across most of England.

mcqs.q: What is the enhanced greenhouse effect?
options: The strengthening of the natural greenhouse effect by human activities (mainly burning fossil fuels) which add CO2 and other gases to the atmosphere.
It is the hole in the ozone layer letting in more sun.
Deforestation has no effect on rivers — only rainfall matters.
The greenhouse effect is entirely man-made and harmful.

mcqs.q: Why does deforestation increase flood risk?
options: Deforestation causes floods because trees normally hold water in their branches forever.
Trees intercept rainfall, their roots increase infiltration and transpiration removes water — removing them increases surface runoff and reduces lag time, peaking river levels faster.
Biotic and abiotic both refer to types of soil.
Deforestation has no effect on rivers — only rainfall matters.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between biotic and abiotic components of an ecosystem?
options: Deforestation has no effect on rivers — only rainfall matters.
Biotic components are all living organisms (plants, animals, microbes); abiotic components are non-living factors (climate, soil, water, light, rock).
Biotic and abiotic both refer to types of soil.
Biotic means animals and abiotic means plants.
